title: False Positive Heroes
description: False Positive Heroes records antivirus false positives and the harm they do to independent developers, publishing VirusTotal observations of {files} files and the cumulative duration of false detections.
headline:
There was no virus.
Still a hit.
intro:
A hall of fame for antivirus engines that flagged perfectly harmless software.
Behind each alarm, an independent developer loses users’ trust and has to start explaining.
award:
Can’t find a threat?
Why not make one up?
awardText:
Where detection counts are read as performance,
even a false alarm goes on the scorecard.
We record those alarms and how they are handled afterwards.

methodTitle: Even one false positive does harm when it lingers.
methodDesc: Before rankings: consistent criteria and verifiable evidence.
m1: {files} files from software the developer has published are monitored through VirusTotal. This is a record of false positives and detection burden on this sample, from the developer’s perspective; it does not represent any engine’s overall performance. Policy-based detections such as PUA and Riskware are also included.
m2: Score = total detection duration across files divided by 24 hours. One file flagged for a day earns one point. Ongoing cases count up to the cutoff. Monthly scores count only duration falling within that month.
m3title: No response does not mean cleared
m3: Duration runs from the first observed detection to the first observation confirming a clean result. Actual onset and clearance times may differ. An engine not responding is not treated as clearance; cases with unconfirmed clearance keep accumulating in the provisional score. Files excluded from monitoring (replaced by a new version or no longer distributed) stop counting at their last scan.
disclaimer: The wording on this page expresses an opinion about an evaluation structure centered on detection counts. It does not assert the intent of any specific vendor. All figures are based on observation records.
missionTitle:
The antivirus: one line of warning.
The developer: dozens of lines of explanation.
missionText:
Users stop downloading. Software gets deleted. The developer is suspected of writing malware. The cost of a false positive falls more on whoever made the software than on whoever raised the alarm.

This page does not evaluate the overall detection performance of any antivirus. It publicly documents misjudgments of legitimate software and the responses that follow, to reduce the harm to independent developers.
